title: Sets
intro: A **set** holds unique values in no particular order: `{"red", "blue"}`. Adding a duplicate does nothing. Sets are fast at answering *is this in here?* and at comparing groups: `|` union, `&` intersection, `-` difference.

questions.prompt: `set(some_list)` removes duplicates. An empty set is `set()` — `{}` makes an empty dictionary.
questions.explanation: Union is *in either*, intersection is *in both*, difference is *in the first but not the second*.

questions.prompt: `visitors` lists every visit to a website, with repeats. Store the number of **different** visitors in `unique_count`.

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert unique_count == len(set(visitors)), 'unique_count should count each visitor once.'

questions.hint: Turn the list into a set, then count.
Duplicates don't count in a set.

questions.prompt: `monday` and `tuesday` list who came to the gym. Store the people who came **both** days in `both_days`, and everyone who came on **either** day in `either_day` (both as sets).
questions.solution:
both_days = set(monday) & set(tuesday)
either_day = set(monday) | set(tuesday)

tests.name: both
tests.code: assert both_days == set(monday) & set(tuesday), 'both_days should be the people in both lists.'

tests.name: either
tests.code: assert either_day == set(monday) | set(tuesday), 'either_day should be everyone in either list.'

questions.explanation: Set operators answer *who was in both?* without writing loops.

questions.prompt: Which of these **can't** go in a set?
questions.explanation: Lists can change, so they can't be set items. Tuples can't change, so they can.

questions.prompt: `seen` should be an empty set, but `add` fails with an *AttributeError*. Fix it.

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert seen == {'x'}, 'seen should be the set {"x"}.'
tests.message: seen should be a set containing x.

questions.hint: `{}` on its own is an empty dictionary.

questions.prompt: Fill in the operator so `new_students` is the students this year who weren't here last year.
questions.hint: *In the first but not the second*.

questions.prompt: Store the different words in `text` as a **sorted list** in `unique_words` (lowercase, split on spaces).
questions.setupCode: text = "The cat saw the dog and the dog saw The cat"

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert unique_words == sorted(set(text.lower().split())), 'unique_words should be the distinct lowercase words, sorted.'

questions.explanation: Sets have no order, so sort them when you need a predictable list.

questions.hint: Does order matter in a set?
questions.explanation: Sets are equal when they hold the same items, in any order.

questions.prompt: A menu checker: `dish` and `allergies` are sets. Store in `safe` whether the dish contains **none** of the allergens, and in `problems` a sorted list of the allergens it does contain.

tests.name: safe
tests.code: assert safe == (not (dish & allergies)), 'safe should be True only if dish and allergies share nothing.'

tests.name: problems
tests.code: assert problems == sorted(dish & allergies), 'problems should be the shared items, sorted.'

questions.hint: `isdisjoint` says whether two sets share nothing. `&` finds what they share.
questions.explanation: Sets make *does this contain any of those?* a one-liner.
